start.text: Ruan. I keep saying it, so it'll stick.
Copper's off. I came up. I don't know what to say to her, so I'm stood here not saying it.
I had a brother. I know that the way you know a tooth's gone. I had his name a while, I think. Somebody said it to me.
I keep coming up here to stand by Wenna. I don't know what for. It feels like the right place to stand.
Somebody'll have to paint the white, come spring. I said I'd go. I've never been out on the Teeth; I'll learn it off the marks.
That's Ruan's name you've got under your arm.

first.text: A lanky lad in a coal-red gansey is levering copper sheets off the bottom of a hauled-up boat with a pry bar, carefully, one nail at a time, stacking each sheet as it comes away.
A ferry. That was a ferry's horn, wasn't it? Nobody's come in since—
Jory Pask. Salvage. This was the Gannet. She's the yard's now. The yard keeps what the sea gives back, every nail. It's what we do.
She was my brother's boat. I had a brother. I know that the way you know a tooth's gone: you keep putting your tongue in the gap.
The Spire went dark on the Keepers' watch, and the Wrack went with it, and the Teeth had the Gannet. That's who drowned him. Whoever he was.

choice.text: Your brother's name was Ruan. Ruan Pask. It's on the Gannet's crew board.
Wenna told me about the night the Gannet came in.
Have you found anything lost? Something good, for a child who keeps lost things.
Did Ruan ever take you out on the Teeth?
The Wrack wants something somebody here holds.

brother.text: Jory stops with the bar under a nail.
Ruan Pask. He'd laugh himself sick, me taking her copper off like a careful old man. He never pulled a nail straight in his life. He'd just— Ruan.

who.text: Wenna knows something. She's sat by that horn ever since and won't let anyone near it. Somebody blew, and somebody answered. So who called them in? The dark? The Keepers?

choice.text: Wenna answered, as she'd answered for fifty years. Then the Wrack went out.
The Spire didn't go out. Keepers put it out, on purpose.
The Wrack went out under them. Nobody's to blame for the dark.

who_wenna.text: Jory looks up the shingle at the old woman by the horn for a long while.
Fifty years. Every boat that ever came home to this hard came home on Wenna's answer. Ruan did, a hundred times.
She answered. Course she answered. She's Wenna.
I'll go up. Not today. I'll get her copper off first. Then I'll go up.

who_keepers.text: Then it was them. I knew it. A Keeper put his hand over the light, and the Teeth had my brother.
He goes back to the copper, harder. The next nail comes out bent.

who_dark.text: The dark. Aye. Nobody's to blame for the dark.
Only it's a hard thing to hate, the dark. I'll keep trying.

float.text: Lost and good? Everything on this hard was lost. Good's harder.
Here. Off the come-home pile. Floats are the one thing the sea always gives back. We keep them a year and a tide for whoever's net they came off, and nobody's come for this one.
He holds out a green glass net-float as big as two fists, in a cage of tarred cord. The sea has frosted it. When you turn it, the grey light goes green inside, like looking up from under a wave.
Tell your finder it's past its year and a tide. It's nobody's. So it's theirs.

teeth.text: Once. I was seven. Bottom of a spring, and Hale painting the white, and Ruan carrying the pot because Hale let him.
Put your feet where the white is, he said. Don't look at the water, look at the white. I did. I never looked up the whole way out.
I remember the white. I don't remember where it was. That's no use to you, is it.

feed.text: Jory sets down the pry bar and wipes his hands, and goes round to the Gannet's open side, and comes back with a small iron pot with a rope bail, crusted white at the lip.
Hale's white-lead pot. I found it wedged under her thwart when I had the boards up. Ruan carried it, the day they took me out. He'd not let me hold it; I'd spill it, he said.
It's what I've got of him that's only mine. Not the yard's. Mine.

He holds it out into the fog that lies over the yard, at arm's length, the way you'd hold a lantern out over the side. He holds it there a long time. The white at the lip goes the grey of everything else.
I remember the white. I never could remember where it was. Maybe it's some use to somebody, the white.

feed_up.text: Ask Wenna. Whatever we give, we'll give it together. She said.

feed_keepers.text: Jory looks at the ember in your hand for the first time as if he's seeing what it is.
That's a Keeper's light. Whatever you are. Same fire as the Spire's, near enough, isn't it?
They put the Spire out on my brother. Not a thing of mine goes in a Keeper's fire. Ask the yard. Ask Wenna. Not me.

pot_back.text: Jory turns the pot round in his hands. The white at its lip has come back, the way it came back on the rocks.
Don't look at the water. Look at the white. Hale said that. Ruan said it after, all the way home, in Hale's voice.
He puts it on the stack of copper, where he can see it.
